claims.text: A delta-learning machine-learning interatomic potential can reliably reproduce the free energies of both solid and liquid states.
The proposed potential can capture vibrational entropy.
The proposed potential can capture anharmonicity.
The proposed potential can capture electron–vibration coupling.
Delta learning will cost substantially less than explicit ab initio molecular dynamics and TOR-TILD workflows.
Relevant elemental and binary metallic systems have previously been studied.
The intervention will refine a baseline empirical potential using a limited set of ab initio molecular-dynamics simulations.
The trained machine-learning potential will be used to calculate free energies for both solid and liquid phases.
The method will retain vibrational and anharmonic effects in its free-energy calculations.
The method is valid approximately from 0.5 to 0.8 times the melting temperature.
The initial applicability domain includes elemental, binary, and moderately complex alloy systems.
Delta learning will produce an improved potential-energy surface that captures cluster-level vibrational behavior, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration coupling.
Learning the energy discrepancy between an inexpensive baseline and ab initio molecular-dynamics data incorporates missing free-energy contributions.
The discrepancy-learning correction drastically reduces computational overhead.
Predicted free energies, melting temperatures, and latent heats will be within approximately 5–10% of explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics results.
The proposed method will require roughly one-tenth the computational cost of explicit methods.
The proposed method will be faster than TOR-TILD.
Explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics and TOR-TILD workflows accurately capture free-energy details but are computationally expensive, especially for multicomponent high-entropy systems.
Extension to highly multicomponent alloys may be limited by sparse training data.

The hypothesis is falsified if melting temperature or latent heat differs by more than approximately 10% from explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics results, or if the method fails to reproduce the specified free-energy contributions.

contradictions.description: The stated operating range of 0.5–0.8 Tm lies entirely below the equilibrium melting point, while the hypothesis and benchmark require solid–liquid fusion free energies at or around Tm. The treatment of the liquid phase outside the stated range is not specified.
